previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with fever, left flank pain, and purulent drainage from his left nephrostomy tube, consistent with a genitourinary tract infection. He had recently completed treatment for a right foot cellulitis. Admission labs showed leukocytosis and elevated creatinine. Imaging revealed decompression of the renal collecting systems without abscess. Cultures from the nephrostomy tube and urine grew Group A Streptococcus and E. coli, guiding antibiotic therapy. Blood cultures showed coagulase-negative staph, likely a contaminant. He was started on meropenem and later transitioned to ertapenem via a PICC line for a two-week course. His infection resolved with normalization of vital signs and labs. A 5 mm left lung nodule was incidentally found on CT, requiring follow-up. He was discharged home with home health services for IV antibiotics and follow-up plans with urology and primary care.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ male paraplegic h/o neurogenic bladder s/p ileal conduit w/
longstanding history of bouts of pyelonephritis, left anastamotic
ureteral-conduit stricture treated with PCNU. Patient presents for routine
exchange.

COMPARISON:   Nephro ureteral stent exchange ___

TECHNIQUE:  OPERATORS: Dr. ___ radiology fellow) and Dr.
___ radiology attending) performed the procedure. The
attending, Dr. ___ was present and supervising throughout the procedure.
ANESTHESIA: Moderate sedation was provided by administrating divided doses of
150 mcg of fentanyl and 3 mg of midazolam throughout the total intra-service
time of 30 min during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were
continuously monitored by an independent trained radiology nurse. 1% lidocaine
was injected in the skin and subcutaneous tissues overlying the access site.
MEDICATIONS: See above
CONTRAST: 30 ml of Optiray contrast.
FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE: 1.47 min, 327 cGycm2

PROCEDURE:  1. Left diagnostic nephrostogram.
2. 8 ___  nephrostomy exchange.

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Following the discussion of the risks, benefits and
alternatives to the procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the
patient. The patient was then brought to the angiography suite and placed
supine on the exam table. A pre-procedure time-out was performed per ___
protocol. The tube site was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.

Diluted contrast was injected into the left catheter to confirm current
position. The image was stored on PACS. Local anesthesia was administered with
instillation of lidocaine jelly and 1% subcutaneous lidocaine injection. The
catheter was cut. A ___ wire was advanced into the catheter and advanced
into the ileostomy. The proximal retaining loop was unformed. The catheter was
removed over the wire.

A new 8 ___ x 22 cm nephroureteral stent was cut at the mid portion of  the
distal pigtail to prevent the catheter from protruding out of the patient's
ileostomy as it was done in the prior procedure. The catheter was advanced
over the wire into appropriate position. The stent was easily advance past the
narrowing at the ureteropelvic junction.  The wire was withdrawn to form a J
loop in the distal catheter. The proximal retention loop was formed and
contrast injection confirmed appropriate positioning. The final image was
saved. The catheter was then flushed. The catheter was secured with 0-silk
suture and a Stat Lock device and sterile dressings. The patient tolerated the
procedure well and there were no immediate post-procedure complications.

FINDINGS: 

1. Left UPJ narrowing.
2. Distal left ureteral stricture at ileostomy anastomosis.
3. Appropriate final position of a left nephroureteral stent.

IMPRESSION: 

Successful exchange of a 8 ___ 22 cm nephroureteral stent on the left,
modified by cutting 2 cm off the tip to prevent pre-catheter from protruding
out of the patient's ileostomy.

ANESTHESIA: Moderate sedation was provided by administrating divided doses of

MEDICATIONS:  Fentanyl, Versed, Meropenam, Zofran
CONTRAST: 20 ml of Optiray contrast.
FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE: 11.02 min, 530 cGycm2

COMPARISON:  Nephroureteral stent exchange dated ___.

FINDINGS: 

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Following the discussion of the risks, benefits and
alternatives to the procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the
patient. The patient was then brought to the angiography suite and placed
supine on the exam table. A pre-procedure time-out was performed per ___
protocol. The tube site was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.
Diluted contrast was injected into the left catheter to confirm correct
position. The image was stored on PACS. Local anesthesia was administered with
instillation of lidocaine jelly and 1% subcutaneous lidocaine injection. The
catheter was cut. A ___ wire was advanced into the catheter and advanced
into the ileostomy and the tube was removed.  A Kumpe catheter was advanced to
the ileal conduit and the ___ wire was exchanged for a Glidewire. The
proximal retaining loop was unformed.  The Glidewire was exchanged for an
Amplatz wire.
A new 8 ___ x 22 cm nephroureteral stent was cut at the mid portion of the
distal pigtail to prevent the catheter from protruding out of the patient's
ileostomy as done in the prior procedure. The catheter was advanced over the
wire into appropriate position. The stent was easily advance past the
narrowing at the ureteropelvic junction. The wire was withdrawn to form a J
loop in the distal catheter. The proximal retention loop was formed and
contrast injection confirmed appropriate positioning. The final image was
saved. The catheter was then flushed. The catheter was secured with 0-silk
suture and a Stat Lock device and sterile dressings. The patient tolerated the
procedure well and there were no immediate post-procedure complications.

IMPRESSION: 

Occlusion of the existing nephroureteral stent. Successful exchange for a new
8 ___ by 22 cm nephroureteral stent.
